title: Drelincourt: memory, thanks for gifts given through her, her faith, her example, and her blessedness
source_text: XXXVII. His consimilia sunt quae de honore quem Beatae Virgini exhibemus, docet Carolus Drelincurtius. Honor, inquit, quem ipsi reddimus in pluribus consistit. Primo enim memoriam illius veneramur, de illa cum omni reverentia loquimur, & plurimum ejus laudibus delectamur. Deinde toto corde, & omnibus animae viribus Deum laudamus propter gratiam & beneficia quae per illam nobis exhibuit. Tertio credimus verba quae ex ejus ore exierunt: fidem & religionem illius amplectimur, & conamur sequi documenta quae Spiritus Sanctus per illud gratiae suae organum nobis reliquit. Praeterea ipsam, ut in bene credendi, ita etiam in bene vivendi exemplum proponimus. Illius pietatem, charitatem, zelum, puritatem, humilitatem, patientiam, constantiam, ac in genere omnes virtutes Christianas, quibus in excellenti gradu ditata fuit, nitimur imitari. Denique beatitudinem ac felicitatem illius extollimus. Libello de honore Beatae Virgini Mariae exhibendo, cap. 2.
pass_a_gloss: Similar to these are the things Charles Drelincourt teaches about the honor we show the Blessed Virgin. The honor, he says, which we render her consists in several things. For first we venerate her memory, we speak of her with all reverence, and we take great delight in her praises. Then with the whole heart and all the powers of the soul we praise God for the grace and benefits which he showed us through her. Third, we believe the words which went out from her mouth: we embrace her faith and religion, and we try to follow the lessons which the Holy Spirit left us through that instrument of his grace. Besides, we set her before us as an example both of believing well and of living well. We strive to imitate her piety, charity, zeal, purity, humility, patience, constancy, and in general all the Christian virtues with which she was enriched in an excellent degree. Finally we extol her blessedness and happiness. In the little book on the honor to be shown the Blessed Virgin Mary, chapter 2.
pass_b_english: Drelincourt's honor of the Virgin begins with reverent memory, speech, and delight in her praises.
Next the whole heart praises God for grace and benefits given through her.
Her words are believed, her faith is embraced, and the Spirit's lessons through her are followed.
She is an example of believing and of living, her Christian virtues are imitated, and her blessedness is extolled.

choices.why: Thanks terminate on God; Mary is the means, not the giver addressed.
rejected: thanks addressed to Mary as giver
